name: Chocolate Charlotte Russe
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ oz. Cooper's gelatine, soaked in a very little cold water
ingredients.originalText: ½ oz. Cooper's gelatine, soaked in a very little cold water

ingredients.name: grated chocolate rubbed smooth in a little milk
ingredients.originalText: 3 tablespoonfuls grated chocolate rubbed smooth in a little milk

instructions.text: Heat the cream to boiling, slowly, stirring frequently
Add the sugar, chocolate, and gelatine, and, when these are dissolved, add, a spoonful at a time, to the beaten yolks
Set back in the saucepan of boiling water, and stir five minutes, until very hot, but do not let it boil
Take it off, flavor, and whip or churn to a standing froth, adding the beaten whites toward the last
Line a mould with cake, fill with the mixture, and set upon the ice

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the cream to boiling, slowly, stirring frequently
2. Add the sugar, chocolate, and gelatine, and, when these are dissolved, add, a spoonful at a time, to the beaten yolks
3. Set back in the saucepan of boiling water, and stir five minutes, until very hot, but do not let it boil
4. Take it off, flavor, and whip or churn to a standing froth, adding the beaten whites toward the last
5. Line a mould with cake, fill with the mixture, and set upon the ice

3 tablespoonfuls grated chocolate rubbed smooth in a little milk
